title: Hearing bands at National Park, lawn parties and parades
summary: As a boy he followed music to National Park and saloons, saw Kid Rena-era bands and Tick Chambers, and notes his musician neighbours including the Correas and Humphreys.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Where did you hear those? At the dances?

I saw them up there, yeah, I heard them at the ballpark, Third and Willa. And they used to have dances there. And I'd hear them at Third and Willa, Six and Willa, wherever there was a saloon. Well you'd hear that music for miles and as kids we'd just start the looping and follow the sound. That was National Park, yeah, Third and Willa, National Park. Punch totals.

That's where I'd hear them. And so there was Tick Chambers, Kohl's, Lawn Parties on Josephine Street. Tick was playing there, you see? So I mean it just was one of those things where you had to hear that music. And on every Monday or Sunday there was advertisement, here comes a horse and wagon, I guess that's where that tailgate come, because the trombone player was always on the end, because he needed room for his slide. So that's why I said I'm very fortunate to have been born in New Orleans and I'm grateful because as a lover of music I came right from the ground floor. I didn't have to go anywhere to hear it, my neighbors was musicians, like the Careers, the Humphreys, and all those people was musicians. But I never studied any music at that time, I just-
How do you spell that name, the Careers, do you remember?
I see, I think it's C-E-R-E-R.
Yeah, C-E-R-E-R-E-R. Yeah, thanks. Something like that. I think it was George Careers.
Yeah, we can look it up in the book.
He was a professor of Careers, yeah. And he had a brother called Sidney that played the tenor saxophone. So before I left New Orleans-
